claims.text: The essay was read to the Royal Society on 23 December 1763 and published in the Philosophical Transactions, volume 53, pages 370 to 418, two years after its author had died on 17 April 1761. It was communicated by Richard Price in a letter to John Canton, and prepared for publication by Price with amendments and additions.

source.title: Bayes, T., An Essay towards Solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances, communicated by Mr Price in a letter to John Canton, Philosophical Transactions 53:370-418, 1763

claims.text: Price was a fellow Nonconformist minister, economist and actuary, to whom the papers had been bequeathed; he found the essay and submitted it to the Society, and believed the theorem offered support for the existence of God.

source.title: Bayes, T., An Essay towards Solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances, communicated by Mr Price in a letter to John Canton, Philosophical Transactions 53:370-418, 1763

claims.text: The arguments were adopted by Laplace, who saw in them the basis for statistical inference, and were later challenged by George Boole. A second paper by the same author, demonstrating the second rule of the essay, appeared in volume 54 pages 296 to 325 and is often missed because the author’s name appears neither in its title nor in the volume index.

beats.broke: the probability of the evidence given a hypothesis and the probability of the hypothesis given the evidence are different numbers, and language provides one phrase for both
beats.fix: relate them explicitly, which forces the third quantity into view — how common the hypothesis was before any evidence arrived
beats.cost: the base rate is frequently unknown, and the calculation then depends on a number you had to supply rather than measure
